chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Durays, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who ordered his slave-girl to enter the state of ihram from a specific time, so she entered ihram while he had not yet entered ihram, and he had intercourse with her after she had entered ihram. He said: He orders her to perform ghusl, then she enters ihram, and there is no penalty upon him. This does not contradict the first report because the way to understand it is to assume that she had not yet recited the talbiyah, for if the matter is so, no penalty is incumbent upon him, as we indicated in the first chapter.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man has intercourse with his slave-girl after she has entered ihram for Hajj but he has not?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *al-Istibsar*, highlighting the juristic principle of reconciling apparent contradictions by distinguishing between the state of intention (*niyyah*) and the formal declaration (*talbiyah*). The master incurs no penalty because the slave-girl’s ihram is considered incomplete without the verbal invocation, a nuance central to Shia fiqh regarding conditional obligations. This reflects the broader Shia methodology of *jam'* (reconciliation) between hadiths by identifying subtle contextual differences.
